raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Builds on #64766 ([this PR's own change](https://github.com/puririshi98/vllm/compare/b12x-nvfp4-w4a16-plan...b12x-nvfp4-w4a16-prefill-fp4)). NVFP4 W4A16 checkpoints run every linear with BF16 activations. Long prefills are compute-bound, and there b12x's FP4 GEMM is 3.3–4.7× faster at 4K–8K rows. This PR adds an opt-in `--kernel-config '{"b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens": N}'`: linear inputs with more than N rows are quantized to NVFP4 with a per-call scale, and smaller inputs, including every CUDA graph replay, stay BF16. It is lossy, so it is off by default.

## Claims

- **Faster long prefills:** at N=1024, 16K-token TTFT drops 1.3× on Bolt (1,772 → 1,336 ms) and 2.6× on Qwen3-32B (5,386 → 2,089 ms). From 1.5K tokens it is also 1.2–1.3× (Bolt) and 2.1–2.8× (Qwen3-32B) faster than Marlin.
- **Decode unchanged:** C=1 inter-token latency is 6.06 vs 6.07 ms on Bolt.
- **Small accuracy cost**, measured with every prefill in FP4 (N=32): MMLU-Pro −0.17 points on Bolt and −0.57 on Qwen3-32B, and both 95% intervals include zero.
- **Prompts at or below N are up to 3.4% slower** on Bolt.
- **Unsafe settings refuse to start:** N below the largest CUDA graph capture size, data parallelism, or encoder CUDA graphs.

## Validation

**End to end:** one RTX PRO 6000, C=1, prefix caching off, TTFT in ms. Bolt is `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB`, Qwen3-32B is `RedHatAI/Qwen3-32B-NVFP4A16`.

| prompt tokens | Bolt, unset | Bolt, N=1024 | Qwen3-32B, unset | Qwen3-32B, N=1024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 768 | 124.6 | 128.8 | 210.8 | 209.3 |
| 1,536 | 184.3 | 148.1 | 416.7 | 118.5 |
| 16,384 | 1,772.1 | 1,335.7 | 5,386.2 | 2,089.3 |

Accuracy with every prefill in FP4 (N=32), deltas vs unset with 95% intervals:

| | Bolt | Qwen3-32B |
|---|---|---|
| MMLU-Pro | −0.17 [−0.56, +0.23] | −0.57 [−1.71, +0.57] |
| perplexity | ×1.005 [×1.003, ×1.007] | ×1.017 [×1.014, ×1.020] |

```bash
# Bolt
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --linear-backend b12x --moe-backend b12x --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --mamba-cache-mode align --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":0,"image":0}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --kernel-config '{"b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens": 1024}'
# Qwen3-32B
vllm serve RedHatAI/Qwen3-32B-NVFP4A16 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --linear-backend b12x --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --kernel-config '{"b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens": 1024}'
# Marlin baseline: either serve command with
#   --kernel-config '{"linear_backend_per_quant": {"nvfp4_w4a16": "marlin"}}'
# TTFT client
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len L --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 12 \
  --num-warmups 2 --max-concurrency 1 --ignore-eos --seed 42
# decode client (inter-token latency)
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 6 --max-concurrency 1 --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` logs no syncs.

**Unit tests** (SM120, b12x 1.5.1; the b12x CI lane is commented out, so these ran locally): `pytest tests/model_executor/kernels/test_b12x_linear.py tests/model_executor/test_b12x_warmup.py` gives 61 passed. On #64766 (`a7a4cfd94`) the same tests give `8 failed, 53 passed`: 7 of the 9 new cases, plus `uses_weight_only_scale_and_a16_dispatch`, which now expects `a16_max_tokens=0`.

```
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_uses_weight_only_scale_and_a16_dispatch
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_does_not_prepare_after_first_call[8]
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_quantizes_activations_above_cutoff[1.0]
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_quantizes_activations_above_cutoff[64.0]
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens_rejects_unsafe_rows[capture_sizes-...]
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens_rejects_unsafe_rows[data_parallel-...]
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens_rejects_unsafe_rows[elastic_ep-...]
FAILED ...::test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens_rejects_unsafe_rows[encoder_cudagraphs-...]
```

Not run: prefix caching on, speculative decoding, TP > 1, SM121, and accuracy on prompts longer than 8K tokens.

## Details

- **Why a custom op:** vLLM compiles with dynamic shapes and does not re-check guards, so a Python branch on the row count would be fixed at trace time. `vllm::b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_linear` picks BF16 or FP4 at run time, from one composite `plan_regimes(..., a16_max_tokens=N)` per layer built at load time as in #64766.
- **One scale per call:** every request in a step above N shares it, including that step's decode tokens, so outputs depend on batch composition, and a non-finite activation makes the whole step non-finite.
- Layers whose per-GPU input size is not a multiple of 128 keep BF16. Docs: `docs/features/quantization/b12x.md`.
- **Relation to #54614 and #54617:** they make the reverse switch, running W4A4 checkpoints as W4A16 at small batches. This PR is for weight-only checkpoints, which have no activation scales.

@@ -35,6 +35,31 @@ force BF16 activations for either FP4 weight format.
 
 The b12x MoE backend does not support expert parallelism, expert maps, EXL3, or NF3.
 
+## NVFP4 W4A16 prefill activations
+
+NVFP4 W4A16 linears keep BF16 activations by default. For long prefills, the
+b12x linear backend can instead quantize the layer input to NVFP4 and run the
+FP4 GEMM. This is lossy, so check accuracy for your model:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> \
+    --linear-backend b12x \
+    --kernel-config '{"b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens": 1024}'
+```
+
+The setting only affects NVFP4 W4A16 linears served by the b12x linear backend.
+Linear inputs with at most `b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens` rows keep BF16
+activations; for most layers, rows are the tokens scheduled in the step. Larger
+inputs are quantized with one NVFP4 global scale per call, computed from their
+absolute maximum and shared by every request in the step. This includes decode
+tokens in such a step, so outputs depend on batch composition. A non-finite
+activation in one request, for example from client-supplied prompt or
+multimodal embeddings, makes the outputs of every request in that step
+non-finite. Smaller values can slow down mid-size prefills. The value must be at
+least the largest CUDA graph capture size; data parallelism and encoder CUDA
+graphs are not supported. Layers whose per-GPU input size is not a multiple of
+128 keep BF16 activations.
+
 ## ModelOpt block codecs

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("a16_max_tokens", [None, 8])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_does_not_prepare_after_first_call(
+    monkeypatch, default_vllm_config, a16_max_tokens
+) -> None:
+    """Every serving token count is planned at load time.
+
+    A b12x preparation evicts programs no prepared plan retains, including
+    routed-MoE kernels compiled earlier in the same forward, which then fails
+    CUDA graph capture. Only the first (profile run) call may prepare.
+    """
+    supported, reason = B12xNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel.is_supported()
+    if not supported:
+        pytest.skip(reason)
+    import b12x.preparation.session as session
+
+    default_vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes = [1, 2, 4, 8]
+    default_vllm_config.kernel_config.b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens = a16_max_tokens
+    k = 256
+    layer, decoded = _nvfp4_w4a16_layer(256, k)
+    kernel = B12xNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel(None)
+    kernel.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+    scheduler = default_vllm_config.scheduler_config
+    capacity = max(
+        scheduler.max_num_batched_tokens, scheduler.max_num_scheduled_tokens or 0, 8
+    )
+    source = torch.zeros(capacity, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    kernel.apply_weights(layer, source)
+
+    prepared = []
+    prepare_default = session.prepare_default
+
+    def record_prepare(request):
+        prepared.append(request)
+        return prepare_default(request)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(session, "prepare_default", record_prepare)
+    for m in (8, 4, 2, 1, 3, 40, capacity + 5):
+        x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        expected = torch.cat(
+            [
+                _nvfp4_activation_reference(chunk, decoded)
+                if a16_max_tokens and chunk.shape[0] > a16_max_tokens
+                else (chunk.double() @ decoded.double().T).bfloat16()
+                for chunk in x.split(capacity)
+            ]
+        )
+        actual = kernel.apply_weights(layer, x)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=0.005, rtol=0.01)
+    assert not prepared
+
+
+def _nvfp4_activation_reference(x, decoded):
+    """Reference output for NVFP4 activations scaled by amax(x), times ``decoded``."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils import (
+        ref_nvfp4_quant,
+    )
+
+    global_scale = 6.0 * 448.0 / x.abs().max().float()
+    codes, block_scale = ref_nvfp4_quant(x, global_scale, 16)
+    dequant = (
+        codes.view(*block_scale.shape, 16) * (block_scale / global_scale)[..., None]
+    )
+    return (dequant.view_as(x).double() @ decoded.double().T).bfloat16()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("magnitude", [1.0, 64.0])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_quantizes_activations_above_cutoff(
+    default_vllm_config, magnitude
+) -> None:
+    """Passes above ``b12x_nvfp4_w4a16_a16_max_tokens`` rows use NVFP4 activations
+    and smaller passes keep BF16 ones, decided at execution time under
+    torch.compile: a branch in traced code would be fixed for every size."""
+    supported, reason = B12xNvFp4W4A16LinearKernel.is_supported()
+    if not supported:
+        pytest.skip(reason)
+    from torch._dynamo.testing import CompileCounterWithBackend
+
+    default_vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes = [1, 2, 4, 8]
+    kernel_config = default_vllm_config.kernel_config
